adelaide-cbd.seoTitle: Adelaide CBD Repairs and Maintenance | Briks
adelaide-cbd.metaDescription: Apartment and heritage building repairs in Adelaide CBD 5000. Leak chasing, strata work and shopfront upkeep organised by Briks for city owners.
adelaide-cbd.h1: Adelaide CBD apartment and shopfront repairs
adelaide-cbd.intro: The city grid stacks offices, shops and apartment towers close together, so a repair on one floor can start with a stain on another. Briks organises independent trades licensed in SA for that kind of work, from a leaking shower above a retail tenancy to a worn shopfront in an older building. You get before and after photos and one invoice.
adelaide-cbd.housing: Adelaide CBD housing includes apartments in towers and conversions, plus shops with flats or offices above them. Buildings include older shopfronts, mid-century offices and later student towers. Wet areas sit over other people's ceilings, services run in shared risers, and facades face dust, heat and summer sun. Some repairs need strata coordination before a trade can start.

trades.note: A leak in an apartment building may not stay in one unit. Water can track through slab edges, shower membranes and shared risers, so the independent plumber Briks arranges may need access to more than one floor to trace the source.

Older shopfronts and converted upper floors can have ageing switchboards, mixed circuits and fluorescent fittings. An independent electrician can test circuits and replace worn cabling in retail and office tenancies.

Shopfront doors, timber window frames and apartment entry doors take heavy daily use. Loose hinges, dropped doors and rotting sills in older facades are the sorts of carpentry jobs Briks arranges here.

Tenant turnover in city apartments brings small jobs: blind brackets, towel rails, door stops, loose handles and patching in strata hallways. These are booked as handyman work rather than a full trade.
Sun and city dust wear exterior paint and shopfront trims. Interior repaints between tenancies can be needed in apartments where walls carry scuffs, patched holes and older paint over plaster.
CBD buildings can have flat or low-pitch roofs with parapets, box gutters and roof-mounted plant. Roofing work in the city can involve blocked box gutters and failed flashings around plant rooms.

issues.title: Summer heat on top-floor units
issues.body: Top-floor apartments under flat roofs take the full summer sun, and ceiling cracks and failed roof membrane seams can show up as stains after a hot spell. The repair can involve tracing the membrane or flashing and fixing it before the next rain.

issues.title: Old shopfront timber and glass
issues.body: Shopfronts from the 1920s to the 1970s can have timber frames, single glazing and painted sills that swell, stick or rot. Repairs can involve easing or replacing frame sections and re-glazing where seals have failed.

issues.title: Tenant leak reports across floors
issues.body: A tenant reports damp on a ceiling that comes from a unit above, and strata needs someone to trace it. The fix starts with checking the shower, bath and riser above, then repairing the failed seal or pipe and making good the ceiling below.

adelaide-cbd.rentals: Rentals here include apartments and small upper-floor flats, some let to students and city workers. Tenants report dripping taps, blocked shower wastes, failed smoke alarms, sticking doors and damp stains from units above.Where a landlord or agency has an approval limit, work beyond it is quoted for approval first.

faqs.q: A tenant says water is coming through the ceiling from the unit above. Who should be told?
faqs.a: Tell the strata manager and the owner of the unit above as well as your tenant, because the source is likely inside another lot. An independent plumber can trace the leak, but access to the upper unit needs to be arranged through its owner or strata.

faqs.q: Our shopfront door has swollen and will not close properly. Can that be fixed without replacing it?
faqs.a: In some cases, yes. Swollen or dropped timber doors can be eased, rehung or have hinges and locks adjusted. If the frame or sill has rotted, the independent carpenter Briks arranges can advise on what needs replacing. Homeowners receive a written quote before work starts.

faqs.q: Who do I call if I smell gas in a city apartment or shop?
faqs.a: Call the Australian Gas Networks faults line on 1800 427 532 first and follow their advice. If anyone is in danger, call 000. Once the line is made safe, a licensed gas fitter can attend to find and repair the fault.

north-adelaide.seoTitle: North Adelaide Repairs and Maintenance | Briks
north-adelaide.metaDescription: North Adelaide 5006 repairs: bluestone terraces, sandstone villas and O'Connell Street heritage fronts need profile-matched materials and careful scoping.
north-adelaide.intro: North Adelaide's streets include bluestone Victorian terraces, sandstone villas and heritage shopfronts along O'Connell Street. The City of Adelaide has heritage controls that affect facade detail. Repairs can need materials and profiles matched to the original, not swapped for the cheapest available option. Briks organises repairs, and independent trades licensed in SA do the work.
north-adelaide.housing: The housing includes early bluestone terraces, late nineteenth to early twentieth century sandstone villas, interwar and post-war infill, plus heritage commercial frontages. Bluestone and soft sandstone move with moisture, lime mortar joints crumble before the stone does, and facade mouldings, cornices and cast iron lacework are hard to match. Repairs go better when the material and profile are identified before anyone starts.

trades.note: Timber sashes, verandah posts, balustrades and external timber trim on the terraces. Joinery on these fronts is often painted hardwood that has soaked up decades of weather and needs like-for-like sections.

Facade painting on bluestone and sandstone needs the right prep: lime-friendly coatings on older render, not a sealed modern skin that traps damp. Cast iron lacework and timber trim take repeated coats.

Slate and older galvanised roofs on the Victorian and Edwardian terraces, plus parapet flashings on larger sandstone buildings. Cracked slates and rusted valley iron can let water into ceilings before a leak is visible inside.
Bathroom and kitchen tiling in the terraces and villas, where floors are often timber or suspended. Tessellated verandah tiles and older bathroom tiles need matching where the original survives.
Old galvanised and copper runs under suspended timber floors, plus damp in subfloor areas. Slow leaks can show up as musty smells or rising damp rather than a burst pipe.

Terraces rewired over the decades can still carry old cotton or early plastic cable in ceilings and behind skirtings. Switchboards in heritage commercial frontages often need attention before new fittings go in.

issues.title: Winter damp in bluestone and sandstone
issues.body: Cold wet winters push moisture into porous bluestone and soft sandstone, and it shows as damp patches, salt bloom and crumbling mortar. Repointing with a lime mortar matched to the original, plus fixing the source of water, is the usual fix rather than sealing the face.

issues.title: Failed mortar and worn facade mouldings
issues.body: Lime mortar joints erode faster than the stone, so rainwater sits in the wall and mouldings and cornices lose their profile. A repair using a compatible mortar mix and matching profile is less likely to trap moisture or change the facade's appearance.

issues.title: Damp and cold rooms in older rentals
issues.body: Damp and cold rooms in terraces and older flats can show as condensation, musty smells and draughty sashes in winter. Addressing ventilation, failed flashings and sash repairs is more appropriate than repainting over the damp.

north-adelaide.rentals: Rental stock here includes terraces, converted villas and flats. Issues can include damp and condensation, sashes that will not close, leaking parapet flashings and tired bathroom tiling.Anything above the agency's approval limit needs approval before work starts.

faqs.q: The bluestone terrace has white salt bloom on the inside wall. What causes it?
faqs.a: Salt bloom comes from moisture moving through the bluestone and mortar and drying on the inside face. The fix is finding where water enters, often a failed flashing, blocked gutter or cracked joint, then repointing with a lime mortar that lets the wall breathe.

faqs.q: Can a damaged sandstone moulding on the facade be matched?
faqs.a: Yes, if the profile is recorded before removal. A carpenter or stonemason can take a template or mould from the surviving section and cut a matching piece in the same stone. Where a section is missing, photos of neighbouring facades help.

faqs.q: The sash windows in the villa rattle and let cold air in. Is that a carpentry job?
faqs.a: It usually is. Sashes that rattle have often lost their parting beads, cords or weights. A carpenter can re-cord, re-bead and ease the sashes so they close properly, which does more for draughts than a temporary seal.

norwood.metaDescription: Norwood 5067 repairs: bluestone cottages and villas near The Parade need carpentry, tiling, paint and gutters. Briks organises independent licensed trades.
norwood.h1: Bluestone and Villa Repairs in Norwood 5067
norwood.intro: Norwood has bluestone cottages, semi-detached villas and old shopfronts converted to homes, with The Parade as the main spine. That mix means repair work on older frontages and small rooms, and on joins where additions meet the original building. Briks organises the work, independent trades licensed in SA do the repairs, and you use one phone number, 0449 517 367, and receive one invoice.
norwood.housing: Houses here were built across many decades, from early stone cottages to later semis, so one street can hold several kinds of construction. Bluestone and lime mortar walls, timber floors, older roofs and small rear additions all show up. Repairs can need to be matched to old materials, and narrow side access on some blocks can change how trades get gear in.

trades.note: Timber sash windows, timber floors and old skirtings in these cottages take knocks, and small rear additions can have timber affected by leaks. A carpenter can free sticking sashes and repair or replace rotted sections.

Lime mortar walls and old rendered fronts need paint that lets the wall breathe; modern acrylics over damp stone can blister. Interior repaints in villas also mean cutting in around deep cornices and picture rails.

Small bathrooms in semis and converted shopfronts can sit over old timber floors, so cracked grout and loose tiles follow movement. A tiler can replace failed bedding and re-grout with a flexible mix suited to the substrate.

Terracotta roofs on these cottages can shed tiles after windy weather, and valley iron can rust where leaves collect behind parapets. A roofer can replace broken tiles, re-bed ridge capping and repair flashings at the chimney.

Narrow eaves and box gutters on shopfront conversions can block with leaf litter from street trees, and the back of the gutter can rust where water sits. Clearing and replacing sections helps protect the stone and render below.

Older Norwood homes can still have galvanised supply lines and clay drains, with wet areas tucked into tight spaces. An independent licensed plumber can trace leaks, replace tapware and repair blocked or cracked drainage.

issues.title: Storm water backing up behind parapets
issues.body: Winter rain on a low parapet or box gutter sends water down the render when an outlet is blocked. The repair is to clear the outlet, check the gutter fall and reseal the joints where the gutter meets the wall.

issues.title: Salt and damp in old bluestone
issues.body: Bluestone and lime mortar hold moisture, so the base of a wall can stay damp and lift paint. A sensible repair is to find where water is getting in, repair the mortar with a lime mix and let the wall dry before repainting.

issues.title: Tenant reports of sticking windows and doors
issues.body: In these rentals, tenants report a sash that will not open or a back door that drags. That can be movement or swollen timber, and a carpenter can plane the door, free the sash and adjust the hardware.

norwood.rentals: Norwood rental homes include cottages and villas. Tenants report sticking windows, leaking taps, blocked drains and worn flyscreens. Landlords and property managers set an approval limit for routine repairs, and anything bigger is quoted for written approval first.

faqs.q: My Norwood cottage wall is damp near the base. What should I do first?
faqs.a: Check the ground outside for a blocked downpipe or garden bed built above the damp course. Water sitting against bluestone is a usual cause. Once the source is cleared, the wall needs to dry before any patch of lime mortar or paint goes back on.

faqs.q: Why do my sash windows stick every winter?
faqs.a: Timber sashes swell in the wet months, and old paint builds up in the runners. A carpenter can free the sash, scrape the runners and fit new cords if needed. Keeping the exterior painted helps limit water getting into the frame.

faqs.q: A tenant says the bathroom tiles are lifting. Who sorts that?
faqs.a: A tiler needs to look at it, because lifting tiles in an older bathroom can mean the bedding has failed over a timber floor. The repair is to remove the loose tiles, check the substrate and re-lay with a flexible adhesive before regrouting.

kent-town.seoTitle: Kent Town Repairs and Maintenance | Briks
kent-town.metaDescription: Kent Town 5067 repairs for warehouses, light industrial sheds and CBD-edge flats: roofing, carpentry, electrical and fit-out fixes organised by Briks.
kent-town.h1: Warehouse and warehouse-conversion repairs in Kent Town
kent-town.intro: Kent Town has converted warehouses, light industrial buildings and high-density flats on the CBD edge. Older industrial buildings sit alongside fit-outs introduced for offices and apartments. Briks organises repairs for owners, landlords and managers here, with independent trades licensed in SA doing the work.
kent-town.housing: The building stock includes former warehouses and light industrial buildings turned into offices and apartments, workshops still in light industrial use, and apartment blocks close to the city. Older industrial roofs, brickwork and windows need maintenance as buildings change use. Fit-outs cut into existing structures, so repairs can involve more than one trade.

trades.note: Converted warehouses can have metal roofs, glazing and skylights. An independent licensed roofer can deal with failed flashings, rusted sheets and leaks over converted office space.
Adaptive reuse work can involve carpentry: new stud walls against brick, door frames set into old openings, and timber floors adjusted in converted warehouses.

Industrial buildings adapted for offices and apartments can have older wiring behind newer fit-outs. An independent licensed electrician can sort switchboard upgrades, added circuits for kitchenettes, and lighting in warehouse ceilings.

Fit-outs add kitchens and bathrooms where there were none, so new pipework ties into old industrial drainage. An independent licensed plumber handles blocked lines, leaking taps and hot water in converted spaces.
Exposed brick, rendered facades and roller doors can show their age on the CBD edge. Painting brickwork, trims and warehouse ceilings can help tidy a fit-out or a shopfront.
Small fixes in mixed-use buildings add up: sticking doors, damaged plasterboard, loose shelving and worn hardware in stairwells and shared entries. A handyman can work through a list of small fixes.

issues.title: Summer heat on warehouse roofs
issues.body: Hot Adelaide summers can affect metal roofs and skylights, and sealant around flashings can dry and crack. Water can then track into converted offices below. Repairs can include resealing flashings, replacing perished washers and clearing roof drainage before heavy rain.

issues.title: Old brickwork and windows
issues.body: Older brick walls and window frames can deteriorate over the decades. Paint can fail, sills can rust and mortar joints can open. Repairs can involve scraping back, treating rust, repointing affected joints and repainting to help keep water out.

issues.title: Tenant fit-outs cutting into old services
issues.body: When a warehouse unit is refitted for a tenant, new partitions and equipment can overload old circuits or block access to drainage. Tenants can then report tripping power or slow drains. Sorting it can mean tracing the services, adding circuits and clearing or rerouting pipework.

kent-town.rentals: Rental properties include apartments, converted warehouse units and small office leases. Issues can include hot water failures, shared drains, tripping circuits and doors affected by fit-out changes.

faqs.q: Can a converted warehouse unit get extra power points without rewiring the whole place?
faqs.a: Yes. An independent licensed electrician can add circuits from the existing switchboard where capacity allows, and only upgrade further if the old board cannot carry the load. The trade assesses the board first, then quotes the additions.

faqs.q: Who fixes a leak coming through a warehouse roof over an office fit-out?
faqs.a: A licensed roofer handles it. Roof glazing, skylights and flashings are possible sources on industrial roofs, and the roofer can identify the failed section and repair it, with before and after photos supplied once the job is done.

faqs.q: Our shopfront brickwork is spalling near the base. What is involved?
faqs.a: Damaged brick at the base can have several causes. A trade can investigate the source of moisture, replace badly damaged bricks, repoint joints and repaint the affected section so the wall can dry.

stepney.metaDescription: Stepney 5069 repairs for converted workshops, townhouses and shops. Briks organises independent trades licensed in SA for plumbing, electrical and repairs.
stepney.h1: Repairs for Stepney's converted workshops and townhouses
stepney.intro: Stepney is a tight inner-east block where old workshops sit between houses, and some of those workshops are now townhouses. The mix means a job can be a bathroom in a converted workshop or a shopfront next door. Briks organises independent trades licensed in SA for both. You call one number, tell us what is happening, and we book the right trade for the work.
stepney.housing: Stepney has older cottages and former workshops, with some workshop buildings converted to homes in recent decades. Brick and stone walls, timber floors and roofs patched over time are part of the mix. On a tight block, access matters: a lane or shared driveway can affect how a job is done. Repairs can involve matching older materials or working around a building that has changed use.

trades.note: Former workshops can have old timber doors and floors. A carpenter can repair a sticking door or replace damaged boards where a former shed is now used as a room.

Corrugated iron roofs on older cottages and former workshops can need repair. Leaks can start at a parapet flashing or where a newer roof meets an older one. A roofer can reseal or replace the flashing.
A townhouse inside an old workshop shell may have new pipework running through old walls. A plumber can trace a leak or fix a tap.
A small shop and a home can share a building. An electrician can sort out a circuit that trips when an old switchboard carries modern loads.
Brick and render on the street frontage, timber and iron at the back. Painting on a tight block can depend on access and prep, especially where an old wall has been patched.
Small jobs in a converted building add up: a sticking door, a loose gutter bracket, a fence paling. A handyman can work through a list without a specialist trade for each item.

issues.title: Summer heat on iron roofs
issues.body: Long hot days push corrugated iron roofs and the ceilings under them. A cracked ridge cap or a dried seal at a flashing can let water in when the first downpour arrives. Fixing the flashing and resealing the joint usually stops it.

issues.title: Old timber in converted workshops
issues.body: Old timber doors and floors in former workshops can be worn or altered. A sticking door or a damaged floorboard may need repair. A carpenter can replace the affected timber and adjust the door or board.

issues.title: Tenants in mixed-use buildings
issues.body: A tenant in a townhouse in a mixed-use building may report noise, a dripping tap or a door that will not latch. The fix can need access through a shared entry or lane. The owner or agency can set a spending limit, and work beyond that limit needs approval first.

stepney.rentals: Rental properties here include townhouses in former workshops, older cottages and some mixed-use buildings. Tenants may report a dripping tap, a door that will not close, or a heater that has stopped.

faqs.q: A tap in my converted workshop townhouse drips and the floorboard under it feels soft. What should I do?
faqs.a: Turn the tap off at the spindle or the nearest isolator and put a bucket under it. A plumber can replace the washer or tap body, and a carpenter can check the floorboard once the leak is stopped. If water has reached a power point, keep clear and call an electrician.

faqs.q: The corrugated iron roof on my old Stepney cottage leaks at the parapet after heavy rain. Who do I book?
faqs.a: Book a roofer. The parapet flashing and the seal at the wall are likely points. A roofer can reseal or replace the flashing. If the leak is near a light fitting or switch, keep away and have an electrician check it after the roof is fixed.

faqs.q: I rent a townhouse in a mixed-use building and the shop's delivery noise comes through the shared wall. Is that a repair?
faqs.a: Not usually a repair. It is a building and use issue. Report it to your property manager so the landlord can look at the shared wall or the shop's hours. If the noise comes with a draught or a gap, a carpenter can check the wall lining and seal.

glenside.metaDescription: Glenside 5065 repairs for interwar bungalows and leafy streets: roof tiles, gutters, sash windows, plaster and rental maintenance, organised by Briks.
glenside.h1: Glenside bungalow repairs, from roof tiles to sash windows
glenside.intro: Glenside's streets have a tight grid of leafy blocks, with interwar bungalows set back behind mature gardens. Briks organises repairs and maintenance for homeowners, landlords and agencies in 5065. Independent trades licensed in SA do the work. Simple problems can be sorted with free phone help before a trade is sent.
glenside.housing: Housing here includes bungalows from the 1920s to the 1940s, with brick or rendered walls, terracotta or concrete roof tiles, timber sash windows and wide eaves. Mature gardens can leave leaf litter in gutters and shade walls that stay damp through winter. Repair work here is likely to involve the roof, gutters, timber windows and internal plaster rather than new fittings.

trades.note: Terracotta and concrete tiles on these roofs crack and slip with age, and the mortar under ridge capping loosens over time. A roofer can replace broken tiles and re-bed loose capping before water reaches the ceiling.
Trees and mature gardens can drop leaves into gutters through autumn. Blocked gutters overflow behind the fascia and into eaves, so clearing and checking the downpipes is sensible before winter.

Timber sash windows, verandah posts and fascia boards in these older houses swell, stick and soften where water sits. A carpenter can repair sashes, replace rotten sections and adjust doors that no longer close squarely.
Older bathrooms and laundries can still have original pipework and fittings. Jobs can include dripping taps, worn washers and slow drains, and checking the hot water service before winter.

Rendered walls and timber trim on older homes take weathering on the south and west sides. Paint that has chalked or blistered can let moisture into the render, so preparing and repainting those faces helps protect the wall.

Original light circuits, ceramic fuses and older power points can turn up in houses of this era. An electrician can check safety switches, replace worn outlets and sort out lighting that trips when several rooms are used at once.

issues.title: Winter damp on south facing walls
issues.body: Shade from mature gardens and cold wet winters can keep south and west walls damp for longer, so paint blisters and mould appears near windows. Work can involve clearing growth back from the wall, checking gutters and downpipes, and repainting once the render has dried.

issues.title: Cracked and slipped roof tiles
issues.body: Terracotta and concrete tiles on these roofs become brittle with age, and mortar under ridge capping cracks. Water then tracks into the ceiling cavity. A roofer can replace the broken tiles, re-bed the capping and check the flashings around chimneys.

issues.title: Tenants reporting jammed sashes and doors
issues.body: Timber frames in older rentals swell in wet weather and stick, which tenants report as a security or ventilation issue. A carpenter can plane and adjust the frame, replace worn catches and repair sash cords rather than replace the whole window.

glenside.rentals: Rental stock here includes older bungalows, so tenant requests can include sticking windows, dripping taps, blocked gutters and heating that struggles in winter. The landlord or agency can agree in advance what repair spending can proceed without further approval; anything beyond that needs their approval first.

faqs.q: The plaster in my 1930s bungalow is crumbling near the ceiling. What causes that?
faqs.a: Crumbling plaster near a ceiling can follow a slow roof or gutter leak. A roofer or plumber should find the water source first, then a plasterer or carpenter can repair the damaged section once it is dry.

faqs.q: A tenant says the sash windows in my Glenside rental won't stay open. Who should look at it?
faqs.a: A carpenter is the right trade for sash windows. Causes can include worn sash cords, loose catches or swollen frames, and these can sometimes be repaired without replacing the window, which keeps the original timber.

faqs.q: Leaves from the street trees keep blocking my gutters. What can be done?
faqs.a: Gutter guards or leaf screens can reduce how much litter settles in the gutter, but they still need checking. A gutter cleaner can clear the gutters and downpipes and tell you whether the fascia or eaves have been damaged by past overflows.

parkside.metaDescription: Older cottages and post-war infill in Parkside 5063. Briks organises plumbing, electrical, carpentry and painting repairs for owners and landlords.
parkside.h1: Parkside 5063: cottages, infill and small repairs
parkside.intro: Parkside's streets combine late nineteenth century cottages with post-war infill on compact blocks, so repair work can bring older materials close to newer fittings. Briks arranges the repair and brings in an independent trade that is licensed in South Australia for the job. Plumbing, electrical, carpentry or painting requests can go through the single phone number.
parkside.housing: Many older cottages in the area use stone or brick with lime mortar, with kitchens and bathrooms updated over time. Post-war infill can sit on small lots close to boundaries, which can make ladder access awkward. Narrow yards, tight side access and street trees can affect how repair work is set up, while roofs, gutters and wet areas are exposed to weather.

trades.note: Older Parkside cottages can have ageing pipework and a mix of fittings. An independent plumber holding SA licensing can trace leaks, replace worn tapware and repair or replace toilet cistern parts.

In post-war infill and updated cottages, older switchboards or limited circuits can need attention. An independent electrician with SA licensing can replace safety switches, add circuits for kitchen updates and check wiring in older wall sections.
For the older cottages, a carpenter can ease sashes that stick, replace decayed sill timber and tighten loose veranda boards as timber moves with seasonal changes.
Roof work on local cottages can include swapping cracked tiles, mending rusted valley sections and fixing flashings that have come loose after leaf litter builds up from street trees.
Gutter work can involve clearing trapped debris, refixing loose runs and changing rusted downpipes so water is directed clear of stone footings and damp subfloors.
Painting work can cover weatherboards, window trims and rendered facades, using a finish that lets stone and lime mortar dry out rather than trapping moisture.

issues.title: Damp in older stone walls
issues.body: In wet cooler months, moisture can enter older stone and lime mortar walls and appear as patches or a musty smell indoors. Clearing blocked gutters, fixing cracked render and letting the wall dry before repainting are the steps to consider.

issues.title: Cracked mortar and render
issues.body: Where lime mortar has softened, damaged render or crumbling joints can let rain into older cottages. Repointing with a compatible mix and patching the render afterwards helps the wall breathe.

issues.title: Doors sticking in rental homes
issues.body: After dry spells or wet weather, timber doors and windows in older rental cottages can stick or swell. Planing edges, adjusting hinges and rehanging the door can keep the original joinery where possible.

parkside.rentals: Parkside rental homes include older cottages and post-war infill. Repair requests can cover sticking windows, dripping taps and gutters that overflow onto paths. Owners or property managers give an approval ceiling for rental work, and jobs above that ceiling are quoted before proceeding.

faqs.q: Who fixes a dripping tap in a Parkside rental cottage?
faqs.a: An independent plumber holding SA licensing can replace the washer or cartridge. Briks books the trade for the repair.

faqs.q: What causes damp patches on the inside of a stone cottage wall?
faqs.a: Water can get into lime mortar through blocked gutters or cracked render and then show inside. The practical sequence is to clear the gutter, repair the render and allow drying before repainting, with Briks arranging the trade.

faqs.q: Can a carpenter fix a sticking timber window in an older Parkside home?
faqs.a: Yes. Timber sashes can swell in wet weather and dry out in summer. A carpenter can plane the frame, adjust hinges or replace worn sash cords so the original window can often be kept.

eastwood.metaDescription: Eastwood 5063 repairs: bluestone semis and 1920s bungalows near Glen Osmond Road. Carpentry, roofing and end-of-lease fixes organised by Briks.
eastwood.h1: Bluestone Semis and Bungalow Repairs, Eastwood
eastwood.intro: Eastwood is a tight pocket of bluestone semis and 1920s bungalows around Glen Osmond Road. Blocks are small, so a repair on one side of a shared wall can affect the neighbour. Briks organises repairs here, arranging for independent trades licensed in SA to do the work. Homeowners can get written quotes, landlords and agencies can set approval limits, and rental jobs can include before and after photos and one invoice.
eastwood.housing: The semis are masonry with narrow frontages and shared party walls. The bungalows that followed in the 1920s often have timber floors and brick chimneys, with small wet areas at the rear. Street trees and seasonal wetting and drying affect older roofs, gutters, mortar and timber.

trades.note: Timber window frames, loose or weathered back verandah beams and sticking doors in the 1920s bungalows, plus floorboard movement where a semi has had damp under the house.
Older roof coverings on the semis and bungalows. Cracked roof coverings, perished pointing and failed flashings around chimneys are among the things a roofing trade can check.
Narrow side passages and street trees mean gutters on these small blocks can fill with leaf litter. Gutters and downpipes need clearing and re-fixing.
Small rear wet areas in bungalows, older pipework under semis and leaking shower recesses. An independent licensed plumber can trace a damp patch back to the trap or the pipe.
Older fuse boxes, aging wiring and additions in kitchens and sleepouts. An independent licensed electrician can check circuits and fit modern safety switches.
Older masonry on the semis and timber trim on the bungalows need preparation suited to the surface. Timber trim can weather on the sun-facing side.

issues.title: Autumn leaf litter in gutters
issues.body: Street trees drop heavily in autumn, and the small blocks here leave little room for water to go anywhere but the gutters. Blocked gutters can back water into the ceiling. Clearing them and checking the outlets and downpipes before winter can help prevent staining inside.

issues.title: Worn mortar on older bluestone walls
issues.body: Older bluestone walls may have mortar joints that wear back over decades. Repointing should be matched to the existing mortar, and a suitably qualified trade can advise on the right approach.

issues.title: End-of-lease wear in small rentals
issues.body: Older semis and bungalows can show sticking windows, dripping taps and doors that no longer latch after a dry summer. These can be small repairs when raised early, and a landlord or agency can set a spending limit for minor items, with work above that limit quoted before it is booked.

eastwood.rentals: Rental stock here includes older semis and bungalows, with maintenance needs such as sticking windows, worn tap washers and doors that swell after rain. For rental jobs, the landlord or agency can set a limit for minor repairs, with work beyond that limit quoted before it is booked.

faqs.q: Who fixes the damp patch on the shared wall of my semi?
faqs.a: Start with an independent licensed plumber, because damp on a party wall can come from a leaking shower, trap or roof flashing rather than the wall itself. Once the source is found and repaired, the plaster and paint can be made good. Talk to the neighbour before work on the shared wall.

faqs.q: My 1920s bungalow has sticking doors every summer. What causes it?
faqs.a: Dry summer air shrinks the timber frames and the doors drop or bind in the jamb. A carpenter can plane and re-hang the door and check the hinges, and it often settles again once the wetter months arrive.

faqs.q: Tree litter keeps blocking the gutter at my roof edge. What can be done?
faqs.a: Clear the gutter before the autumn drop and again after it, and check the outlets and downpipes are open. A gutter guard can reduce how much gets in. If water has already stained the ceiling, the roofing or gutters trade can check the flashing and the gutter fall.

magill.metaDescription: Older stone and 1950s brick veneer homes along Magill Road, 5072. Briks organises repairs for local homes with independent trades licensed in SA.
magill.h1: Magill stone and brick veneer repairs, 5072
magill.intro: Magill stretches along Magill Road from the inner east towards the foothills, with a mix of housing along the way. Some 1920s stone cottages sit near 1950s brick veneer homes, so repair work varies from property to property. Briks organises repairs for both; independent trades licensed in SA do the work.
magill.housing: Older stone houses along Magill Road vary in construction, so repairs should be matched to the building. Some 1950s brick veneer homes have older roof tiles, gutters and timber windows that may need attention. Magill is inland, with hot dry summers and cooler wet winters near the foothills.

trades.note: Timber work in older Magill houses can involve window frames, doors and skirtings. A carpenter can repair or replace these while leaving sound stonework alone.
Some roofs on 1950s brick veneer homes have cracked tiles and loose ridge capping. A roofer can replace damaged tiles and reset capping before winter rain.
In older stone houses, pipework can be hard to follow, so a leak may appear away from its source. A plumber can trace it and deal with old galvanised lines or worn tapware.
Gutters along Magill Road can collect leaf litter from street trees and block at joints. Clearing and repairing gutters and downpipes helps direct water away from the house.
Sun can fade and chalk paint on west-facing weatherboards and rendered fronts. A painter can prepare and recoat before the surface breaks down further.
Houses from the 1920s to the 1950s can still have old wiring or a dated switchboard. An electrician can check circuits, replace worn fittings and add safety switches where needed.

issues.title: Cracked stone after a dry summer
issues.body: After long dry summers, hairline cracks can show in older stone and cornices. A tradesperson can advise on repointing with a matching mortar and patching internal cracks. Check again after the first heavy autumn rain.

issues.title: Tiles slipping on older roofs
issues.body: Some 1950s brick veneer roofs have cracked tiles and lifted ridge capping. Water can then reach ceiling spaces. Replacing broken tiles and repointing the capping can be done before winter.

issues.title: Tenants reporting damp in stone walls
issues.body: Rentals in older stone cottages can show damp inside during wet weather, and tenants may notice musty rooms or peeling paint. Clearing blocked gutters, repairing failed downpipes and improving subfloor ventilation can help.

magill.rentals: Rental homes in Magill include older stone cottages and 1950s brick veneer houses. Maintenance requests can cover gutters, taps, doors and hot water units. The landlord or agency gives an approval limit, and work beyond that limit is quoted before it proceeds.

faqs.q: Our 1920s stone cottage near Magill Road has damp patches in winter. What should we look at first?
faqs.a: Look at the gutters and downpipes first. Overflowing gutters or a broken downpipe can let water into an older stone house. Clearing the gutters, repairing the downpipe and checking subfloor ventilation can help.

faqs.q: The tiles on our 1950s brick veneer roof look worn. Can that wait until spring?
faqs.a: If no water is coming in, it may wait, but cracked tiles and lifted ridge capping can let rain into the ceiling during winter. A roofer can replace damaged tiles and reset the capping. The job includes before and after photos once complete.

faqs.q: I rent out a stone cottage in Magill and the tenant says a door is sticking. Who handles it?
faqs.a: A sticking door in an older stone house can be caused by seasonal movement or a swollen frame. A handyman or carpenter can plane and refit it. You can give an approval limit; any work beyond it is quoted before it starts.

burnside.metaDescription: Sandstone villas in Burnside 5066 need careful repairs. Briks organises independent trades licensed in SA for roofs, gutters, painting and storm damage.
burnside.intro: Burnside has streets with mature plane trees and sandstone villas. Older materials such as lime mortar, timber joinery and slate or terracotta roofs need care when repairs are planned. For Burnside jobs, Briks organises the repair, and an independent trade licensed in SA does the work. When the work is finished, you receive before and after photos and one invoice.
burnside.housing: Houses here include late 1800s stone villas and return verandah cottages through to interwar and post-war homes. Sandstone, lime mortar, timber joinery and terracotta or slate roofs appear across the area. On the foothills side, runoff from larger roofs can be significant, and mature trees drop leaf litter into gutters. Repairs to older details need care rather than quick patches.

trades.note: Terracotta and slate roofs on older Burnside villas can be damaged by wind and hail. Repairs can involve cracked tiles, lifted slate and worn valley flashings, and matching old profiles takes care.

Leaf litter from plane trees and established gardens can block gutters and valley gutters. Blocked downpipes can then push water into eaves and cornices, so clearing the gutter and checking the timber fascia matters here.
Timber fascias, barge boards and verandah posts on sandstone villas weather over time. Paint that has chalked off can expose bare timber, and lime mortar joints may need repointing before painting.
Older Burnside homes can have timber floors, sash windows and verandah structures. Sticking sashes, rotted sill boards and worn verandah boards are examples of work for an independent carpenter.
Stone villas can have ageing pipework and older bathroom wet areas. Dripping taps, leaking shower recesses and worn roof plumbing are examples of work for an independent plumber licensed in SA.

Older houses here can have outdated switchboards, ceramic fuses and added circuits. Safety switches, outdoor lighting and fault finding are examples of work for an independent electrician licensed in SA.

issues.title: Stormwater from larger roofs
issues.body: Larger roofs shed a lot of water in a downpour. If gutters hold plane tree litter or a valley flashing has lifted, water can get into eaves and cornices. Clearing gutters and repairing flashings can reduce this risk.

issues.title: Lime mortar and stone faces
issues.body: Sandstone villas were built with lime mortar, which is softer than modern cement. Cement pointing can trap moisture and damage the stone face. Repointing with a compatible lime mix is one repair option, allowing the wall to dry out.

issues.title: Tenant reports on older wet areas
issues.body: Rentals in Burnside can be older villas with original or updated bathrooms. Tenants may report leaking showers, mould on cornices and dripping taps. An independent plumber licensed in SA can check the shower recess and tapware, and the repair is then arranged with photos sent to the owner.

burnside.rentals: Burnside rentals include older villas and updated family homes. Tenant requests can involve wet areas such as leaking shower recesses, ceiling mould and dripping taps, along with blocked gutters after rain. For rental work, the owner or property manager decides what can proceed without a separate quote; work beyond that limit is quoted first.

faqs.q: Who fixes a leaking shower in an older Burnside villa?
faqs.a: An independent plumber licensed in SA does the work. They check the shower recess, tapware and tiled junctions, then explain what the repair involves. Briks arranges the booking, then passes on before and after photos and a single invoice after the repair.

faqs.q: The plane trees keep filling my gutters. What should I do?
faqs.a: Have the gutters and downpipes cleared before the wet months, then checked again after leaf drop. If water has already stained the eaves or cornices, ask for the fascia and valley flashings to be looked at as well, because litter and blocked outlets can be the cause.

faqs.q: Can a sandstone wall be repointed with normal cement?
faqs.a: It is better not to. Lime mortar is softer and lets the wall breathe, while cement pointing can trap moisture and damage the stone face. A tradesperson familiar with older stonework can match the mix to what is already there.

beulah-park.metaDescription: Beulah Park 5067 local repairs for character cottages and villas: roofing, gutters, carpentry and end-of-lease work organised by Briks.
beulah-park.intro: Beulah Park is a compact pocket of character cottages and older villas between Norwood and Burnside, with the old railway line part of its history. Some homes date from the late 1800s or early 1900s, and their timber, masonry and rooflines show the effects of age. Briks organises repairs here, booking independent trades licensed in SA for each job.
beulah-park.housing: The housing stock runs from late 1800s cottages through to 1920s and 1930s bungalows, with later infill. Walls can be brick or stone, roofs corrugated iron or terracotta tile, and windows timber sash. Inland weather brings hot dry summers and cool wet winters, so paint breakdown and gutter overflow can affect houses of this age.

trades.note: On older cottages, corrugated iron may have had repeated patch repairs. An independent roofer can check loose sheets, perished washers and cracked tiles on bungalows.
Box gutters and fascia runs on villas can collect leaf litter. Overflow can track back into eaves and masonry, so clearing and re-fixing matter.
Timber sash windows, front doors and verandah posts weather over time. Sticking sashes, rotted sill sections and loose balustrades are carpentry items an independent carpenter can handle.
Paint on timber trim and render of older homes can break down, especially on sun-facing walls. Preparation matters when the surface is weathered weatherboard or masonry.
Older cottages can have ageing pipework under the floor. Dripping taps, leaking cisterns and slow drains are plumbing items an independent licensed plumber can address.
Switchboards in interwar and older homes may not suit modern loads. An independent licensed electrician can check old wiring, replace worn GPOs and check safety switches.

issues.title: Hot summer on iron roofs
issues.body: Dry summer heat can expand corrugated iron against its fixings. Loose screws and worn washers can let water in when winter rain returns. A roofer can re-screw sheets and replace perished washers.

issues.title: Masonry paint and mortar
issues.body: Older masonry walls can have paint breakdown and loose mortar after years of weather. A trade can match materials to the existing wall for repointing or painting.

issues.title: End-of-lease repairs in cottages
issues.body: End-of-lease lists in older cottages can include sticking doors, worn flyscreens, dripping taps and sash windows that will not close. A handyman or the appropriate trade can work through the list.

beulah-park.rentals: Rental properties here can include older cottages and villas. Repair lists can mention jammed sash windows, dripping taps, worn flyscreens and gutters that overflow in winter. Rental approvals are handled by the owner or property manager: their limit decides what can go ahead, and jobs beyond it are quoted first.

faqs.q: Who fixes a leaking iron roof on an old Beulah Park cottage?
faqs.a: An independent licensed roofer can. Briks can book the trade; for homeowners, a written quote is provided before work starts. The roofer can check sheets, screws and flashings and repair what is letting water in.

faqs.q: Can a handyman deal with sticking sash windows in these cottages?
faqs.a: In some cases. A handyman can free painted-shut sashes, replace cords and adjust catches. If the frame or sill is rotten, a carpenter is the better booking, and Briks can arrange that.

faqs.q: What should I do if I smell gas in my Beulah Park home?
faqs.a: Leave the property and call Australian Gas Networks faults line on 1800 427 532. If anyone is in danger, call 000 first. After the line is made safe, Briks can book an independent licensed gas fitter to find and repair the fault.

glenunga.metaDescription: Bungalow-era Glenunga 5064: kitchen and bathroom updates, tiled roofs, sash windows and rental repairs; Briks organises independent trades licensed in SA.
glenunga.h1: Glenunga bungalow repairs and kitchen updates
glenunga.intro: Glenunga's streets are quiet and lined with interwar bungalows and post-war family homes, some within walking distance of Glenunga International School. The school is a local anchor, and family homes can need kitchen and bathroom updates. Briks organises independent trades licensed in SA for that work, from a tired bathroom to a leaking roof valley, and keeps the paperwork to one invoice.
glenunga.housing: The housing here runs from 1920s and 1930s bungalows with brick fronts, timber sashes and terracotta tile roofs through to 1950s and 1960s brick homes on generous blocks. The inland setting means hot dry summers and cool wet winters, so roofs, gutters and timber take a beating. Older kitchens and bathrooms in these houses may need rework.

trades.note: Timber window frames, skirting and door jambs in the older bungalows here dry out and swell with the seasons. A carpenter can free a sticking sash, replace rotted sill timber or refit a door that no longer closes.

Bathroom and kitchen retiling in these 1930s to 1960s homes can mean stripping old tile beds back to the wall and re-sheeting before new tiles go on. Floor tiling in laundry areas is another job that comes up.

Older Glenunga bathrooms and kitchens can still have original galvanised or early copper pipework, plus tired tapware and waste traps. An independent licensed plumber can sort leaks, replace a vanity or rework the supply to a new kitchen layout.

Terracotta tiles on the bungalows can crack and slip, and the valleys and flashings around chimneys can take water in wet winters. Roofing work here can include repointing ridge caps, replacing broken tiles and clearing a valley that has silted up.

Kitchen and bathroom reworks can need new circuits, more power points and safer bathroom lighting. Older homes here can still carry ceramic fuses and ageing switchboards, which an independent licensed electrician can check and update as part of the job.

Fascias, window trims and any weatherboards on these houses can fade and chalk in the summer sun. Exterior repainting, plus patching and repainting a renovated kitchen or bathroom, is the sort of work that follows a renovation.

issues.title: Winter water at the chimney flashing
issues.body: When the winter rain sets in, water can track past old chimney flashings and valley iron on tiled roofs, showing up as a stain on a ceiling. The fix can be repointing, new flashing or replacing cracked tiles, with the ceiling patch made good afterwards.

issues.title: Sash windows painted shut
issues.body: Timber double hung windows in bungalows this age seize up when paint bridges the frame and the cords perish. A carpenter can free the sash, replace the cords and re-putty loose glass, which restores ventilation to a bedroom or kitchen without replacing the window.

issues.title: Tenants report tired bathroom fittings
issues.body: In rental houses here, tenants may raise dripping taps, a toilet that runs, mould at the shower base or a vanity that has swollen. Repairs range from new washers and silicone to replacing the vanity or resealing the shower, depending on what the trade finds.

glenunga.rentals: Rental properties here include older three and four bedroom homes. Tenants may report issues with bathroom and kitchen fittings, hot water, heating and cooling, and gutter or roof leaks after winter rain.If a job exceeds the approval limit agreed with the landlord or agency, approval is needed before work proceeds.

faqs.q: Our Glenunga bathroom is original to the house. Can it be updated without a full rebuild?
faqs.a: It can be, depending on what is behind the tiles. If the wall sheeting and pipework are sound, retiling, new tapware and a new vanity can lift the room. If the shower base or pipework has failed, the trade will say so and the job grows from there.

faqs.q: We are near the school and trees drop leaves. How should gutters be handled?
faqs.a: Clear them before the winter rains and check them again after a windy spell. On these older homes the gutter can feed a valley or a downpipe that blocks easily. A roofing or gutter trade can clear the run, check the brackets and replace rusted sections of gutter.

faqs.q: The kitchen in our 1950s home has one power point. Can more be added?
faqs.a: Yes, an independent licensed electrician can add circuits and outlets, but the switchboard needs to be able to take them. In homes this age the board may still have old fuses. The electrician will check the board and earthing and quote the upgrade alongside the kitchen work.

toorak-gardens.seoTitle: Toorak Gardens Repairs and Maintenance | Briks
toorak-gardens.metaDescription: Toorak Gardens 5065 repairs for large interwar villas and mature gardens: carpentry, roofing, painting, gutters, tiling and plumbing booked by Briks.
toorak-gardens.intro: Toorak Gardens is a pocket of large interwar villas set among mature gardens, where the work is often heritage-respect renovation. Jobs here tend to run for weeks and pull in several trades in turn. Briks organises that work and books independent licensed trades for each part. One number, one invoice at the end.
toorak-gardens.housing: The villas here went up mainly between the 1910s and the 1930s, in brick and render with terracotta tile roofs, tall ceilings and wide eaves. Some retain leadlight, timber sash windows and lime mortar joints. Mature gardens mean leaf litter on roofs and gutters and shaded walls that stay damp through winter. Roofs, gutters and joinery are areas where wear shows.

trades.note: Timber sash windows, verandah posts, fascia and barge boards on these interwar villas take the weather on the south side. An independent carpenter can repair sashes, replace rotted frames and rehang doors that have moved with the seasons.

Terracotta tile roofs from the 1920s and 1930s crack and slip, and valley irons rust under the leaf litter from the big garden trees. A roofer can replace cracked tiles, re-bed ridge capping and deal with the flashings around chimneys.

Deep eaves and tall garden trees fill gutters fast here. Box gutters and quad gutters on these villas overflow into the eaves lining when they block, so clearing and re-fixing sagging runs is part of autumn maintenance.

Render and lime mortar walls need to breathe, so paint choice matters on these older villas. Weatherboard and timber trim on the shaded south elevation can hold moisture. A painter can prepare properly and repaint fascias, barge boards and window frames.

Original bathrooms in these villas may have small mosaic floor tiles and wall tiles that have lifted from movement. A tiler can retile a bathroom floor, replace a shower base and match tiles in older wet areas where the existing stock allows.

Old galvanised and copper pipe runs under these large villas can show up as damp patches and low pressure at the far tap. A licensed plumber can trace a leak, replace a run of pipe and sort out the stormwater downpipes that tie into the garden.

issues.title: Autumn leaf litter in box gutters
issues.body: Trees in these gardens drop heavily in autumn, and box gutters on the wide-eaved villas block quickly. Water then backs up under the tiles and stains eaves lining. Clearing the gutters and checking the downpipes before winter rain is the usual fix.

issues.title: Cracked terracotta tiles on old roofs
issues.body: Roof tiles from the 1920s and 1930s crack along the ridge and where people have walked on them. Moss grows in the shaded valleys. Replacing the cracked tiles, re-bedding ridge capping and clearing valleys can deal with the leaks that show as ceiling stains.

issues.title: Tenant reports of damp in older villas
issues.body: Renters in these big villas may report damp on the south wall or around a bathroom window, where render and lime mortar hold moisture in winter. The usual approach is to check the roof and gutter first, then the ventilation and paint on that elevation.

toorak-gardens.rentals: Rental properties here include larger villas and some subdivided flats, let to tenants who notice damp, cold rooms and older bathroom fittings. Reports are often about a leaking shower, a sticking window or a downpipe that has come away.

faqs.q: Our 1920s villa has damp on the south wall each winter. What should we check first?
faqs.a: Check the roof and the box gutter above that wall before anything else. Blocked gutters and cracked tiles are a possible source, and water can track down inside the wall. Once that is clear, look at the paint and ventilation on that shaded elevation.

faqs.q: The terracotta roof on our Toorak Gardens house has slipped tiles after a hot summer. Can they be replaced?
faqs.a: Yes. Cracked and slipped terracotta tiles can be replaced and the ridge capping re-bedded. A roofer can match tiles as closely as the existing stock allows and check the valley irons and chimney flashings while they are up there.

faqs.q: We are renovating a villa and need several trades over a few weeks. How does that work?
faqs.a: Briks organises the job and books each independent licensed trade in the order the work needs to run, so carpentry, roofing and painting can follow one another. Homeowners get a written quote before work starts, and finished jobs come with before and after photos and one invoice from Briks.

marryatville.metaDescription: Bungalow repairs in Marryatville 5068: tiled roofs, timber sashes and big-tree gutters on the leafy streets between The Parade and Kensington Road.
marryatville.intro: Marryatville's tight leafy streets are lined with bungalows and villas set behind mature trees, and many have been extended or reworked at the back. That mix of old roof and new addition is where a lot of repair work starts. Briks organises the trades for these jobs, arranging independent licensed tradespeople for each part, with before and after photos and one invoice.
marryatville.housing: The stock here runs from nineteenth-century cottages and villas through to interwar bungalows, with weatherboard, brick and rendered masonry walls under terracotta or zincalume roofs. Big trees overhang many blocks, so gutters fill and roof edges take shade and damp. Renovated backs add modern fittings to old shells, so repairs often cross both.

trades.note: Terracotta tiles and older zincalume sheets sit under heavy tree cover here, so cracked tiles, lifted flashing and worn valleys turn up on bungalow roofs and rear extensions.
Leaf litter from the big street trees blocks gutters and box gutters on these bungalows, and overflowing water shows up as damp on fascia boards and eaves linings.
Timber sash windows, verandah posts and fascia boards on the older villas take weather and movement, so eased sashes, rotten post bases and loose boards are repair jobs.
Older bungalows here often have original galvanised pipe and dated bathroom fittings, while renovated backs run new copper and PVC, so leaks can sit at the join between the two.
Rewired front rooms and newer rear additions can leave mixed circuits and old ceramic fuses in the same house, so switchboard and outlet faults need a licensed electrician.
Rendered and weatherboard walls under the tree canopy hold moisture and go chalky, so prep and repainting of trim, eaves and pickets helps protect the timber.

issues.title: Gutter overflow after autumn leaf fall
issues.body: The big trees drop heavily over the gutters and box gutters on these bungalows. When gutters block, water backs up under the eaves and stains fascia boards and ceilings. Clearing and checking the fall of the gutter, then refixing loose brackets, usually sorts it.

issues.title: Cracked terracotta on shaded roof slopes
issues.body: Terracotta tiles on south-facing slopes stay damp longer under the trees, and cracked or slipped tiles let water into the roof space. A roofer can replace the broken tiles, check the flashing and valleys, and clear the debris holding moisture.

issues.title: Damp in an old rear bathroom
issues.body: An older bathroom, or one added into a rear extension, can develop mould and peeling paint around the shower. The fix is usually resealing, checking the exhaust and repairing any leak behind the tiles.

marryatville.rentals: Rentals in Marryatville include older bungalows and villas, some extended at the back. Damp bathrooms, sticking sashes and gutters overflowing after leaf fall can come up. Where a landlord or agency has agreed an approval ceiling in advance, work above that ceiling is quoted before it goes ahead.

faqs.q: Who fixes a sash window that won't close before winter in an old Marryatville bungalow?
faqs.a: A carpenter handles a sticking or dropped timber sash. The usual fix is to free the sash, replace worn cords or balances, and adjust the frame so it closes against the reveal. If the sill or frame has rot, that is a separate carpentry repair.

faqs.q: My gutters overflow in the front of the house but not the back. What is going on?
faqs.a: The front gutters take a heavier leaf load from the street trees, so they block first. A gutter trade can clear them, check the brackets and fall, and confirm the downpipes are running. Overflow that stains the eaves usually points to a blocked downpipe rather than the gutter itself.

faqs.q: There is mould around the shower in a rear extension. What should I do?
faqs.a: Treat it as a leak and ventilation problem, not just a cleaning job. An independent licensed plumber can check the shower waste and tapware, and a tiler can reseal or repair failed grout and silicone. Improving the exhaust fan can also help reduce the chance of it returning.

erindale.metaDescription: Brick veneer and townhouse repairs in Erindale 5066, east of Burnside. AC retrofits, hot water swaps and the small jobs mid-century homes need.
erindale.h1: Erindale brick veneer and townhouse repairs, 5066
erindale.intro: Erindale is a quiet pocket east of Burnside where mid-century brick veneer houses sit alongside newer infill townhouses. Repairs here tend to involve services and fittings. Briks organises those jobs, and independent trades licensed in SA do the work. Homeowners receive a written quote, and before and after photos and one invoice are provided.
erindale.housing: The older houses here are often single storey brick veneer from the decades after the war, with timber floors, terracotta or concrete roof tiles and original wiring and plumbing in some. Newer infill townhouses add a different mix of fittings and tighter service spaces. That mix means a repair in Erindale can start with finding where a pipe or cable runs.

trades.note: The older brick veneer houses here often still run one wall-mounted unit or an old evaporative cooler on the roof. Adding a split system to a back bedroom usually means a new circuit and a wall penetration through brick.

Original copper and old galvanised lines turn up in the mid-century houses, and hot water units in these homes are often tucked into a laundry or a tight side path. A swap-out needs the same footprint or a rethink of the cupboard.

Switchboards in the older Erindale houses can still hold ceramic fuses, and the wiring predates the load of a modern kitchen. Adding circuits for an oven or an air-conditioner usually starts at the board.

Concrete roof tiles on the post-war houses crack and lose their bedding over time, and the low-pitch carport roofs on the townhouses can pond water. Repointing and replacing cracked tiles is the usual fix.
Gutter runs on these homes can block with leaf litter from nearby gardens. Sagging brackets on the older fascia boards let water track back into the eaves.
Infill townhouses come with hollow-core doors, sliding robe tracks and flyscreens that wear out quickly with a family in them. The older houses need sticking windows and worn cupboard hinges sorted.

issues.title: Summer heat and old air-conditioners
issues.body: The inland position here means hot, dry summers, and older units in these houses work hard through them. When a unit stops cooling, the fix is usually a gas top-up, a capacitor or a blocked condenser coil, and sometimes a straight replacement with a more efficient split system.

issues.title: Cracked tiles on post-war roofs
issues.body: Concrete tiles from the mid-century houses go brittle and crack after decades of sun, and the mortar bedding under the ridge caps breaks down. Replacing the cracked tiles and repointing the ridges keeps water out of the ceiling space before it reaches the cornices.

issues.title: Tenant hot water and appliance faults
issues.body: Tenants in Erindale's townhouses and older rentals report hot water failing, heaters tripping and doors that no longer latch. A licensed plumber or electrician checks the unit and the circuit, and the owner or agency is given a quote before work beyond the approval limit goes ahead.

erindale.rentals: The rental stock here is a mix of original brick veneer homes and the newer townhouses, and tenants typically ring about hot water, heating and small door and screen faults. For rentals, the owner or agency can set how much can be approved without a quote; work beyond that is quoted first.

faqs.q: My 1960s brick veneer in Erindale has hairline cracks above the windows. What causes that?
faqs.a: Movement in the brickwork and timber frame as the soil dries and swells over the seasons. Fine cracks in the mortar can be patched and monitored, and if they widen or run through the brick itself, a licensed tradesperson should look before you patch over it.

faqs.q: Can I put a split system in a townhouse bedroom here without a big renovation?
faqs.a: Often yes. The indoor unit goes on an external wall, the outdoor unit sits on a bracket or a small pad, and a licensed electrician runs a circuit from the switchboard. In a townhouse the main question is where the outdoor unit can sit without bothering neighbours.

faqs.q: The hot water in my Erindale rental is lukewarm. Who should I call?
faqs.a: Call Briks on 0449 517 367 and describe it. A licensed plumber checks whether it is the element, the thermostat or the tank itself, and for a rental the owner or agency is given the likely cost before a replacement unit is booked in.

rosslyn-park.seoTitle: Rosslyn Park Repairs and Maintenance | Briks
rosslyn-park.metaDescription: Split-level homes on Rosslyn Park's sloping foothill blocks, 5072. Repairs for retaining walls, drainage, roof lines and gutters before the wet season.
rosslyn-park.h1: Sloping Block Repairs in Rosslyn Park
rosslyn-park.intro: Rosslyn Park climbs from the eastern plains into the foothills, and many homes sit on split levels cut into the slope. That shape puts water and ground movement at the centre of repair work. Briks organises repairs by independent trades licensed in SA for homeowners, landlords and property managers here. Homeowners get a written quote before work starts, and jobs finish with before and after photos and one invoice.
rosslyn-park.housing: The foothill edge means many blocks slope, so houses built from the 1950s onward can be arranged on split levels or stepped down the slope. Winter rain runs to the low side of each block, and roofs can take wind from the hills. Repairs tend to follow water: blocked ag drains, cracked path edges, damp along a lower wall and gutters that overflow at a valley.

trades.note: On sloping blocks the stormwater line is the first thing to check. An independent licensed plumber can trace where the ag drain discharges, clear silt from a pit and repair a cracked PVC line before winter rain finds the lower wall.

Split-level homes here can have timber decks, stair treads and balustrades on the downhill side. Damp and movement can loosen stringers and handrails. An independent licensed carpenter can re-fix treads, replace rotted decking boards and tighten balustrade posts.

Steep tiled roofs on the ridge line take wind and leaf litter from the hills. Cracked ridge capping and lifted tiles show up after a windy spring. An independent licensed roofer can re-bed and point ridge caps and replace broken tiles on the uphill face.

Box gutters and valley irons on split-level roofs collect leaf litter. When a valley blocks, water backs under the fascia. An independent licensed gutter trade can clear valleys, re-fix sagging brackets and replace rusted sections of metal gutter.

Timber fascias and window reveals on the weather side of these homes take sun and wind from the hills. Paint chalks and flakes on the north and west faces. An independent painter can prepare and repaint fascia boards, barge boards and the lower weatherboards.

issues.title: Winter runoff on the low side
