Older cottages can carry a mix of old wiring and newer additions, and damp hills winters can expose weak spots. Safety switches, outdoor lighting circuits and power to sheds or pumps are the jobs an independent licensed electrician is booked for.

issues.title: Autumn leaf litter blocks gutters
issues.body: When the eucalypts shed in autumn, gutters and valleys can fill quickly, and the first heavy winter rain can find the overflow. Water can then track behind fascia boards and into eaves. Clearing the gutters and checking the downpipes before the wet season is a practical step, with guards fitted where the trees are close.

issues.title: Lime mortar in old stone walls
issues.body: Older stone cottages often use lime mortar, which stays soft and lets the walls breathe. Repointing with hard cement mortar can trap moisture and damage the stone face. A trade who works with stone should assess the joints and use a matching lime mix rather than cement.

issues.title: Winter damp in older rentals
issues.body: Rentals in Crafers can be cold and damp through winter, with condensation, mould and draughts around old windows. Fixes can include clearing blocked subfloor vents, repairing failed flashings and sealing or rehanging timber windows.

crafers.rentals: Rental stock here includes older cottages and family homes on large blocks; winter damp, cold and gutter issues can arise. For rentals, the landlord or property manager agrees the approval threshold, and work above that threshold needs approval before it proceeds.

faqs.q: Does a Crafers house need anything special for bushfire season?
faqs.a: Keeping gutters and roof valleys clear of leaf litter and repairing failed flashings are practical maintenance steps for bushfire season. If anyone is in danger during a fire, call 000 first.

faqs.q: My stone cottage has crumbling mortar between the stones. Can it be repointed?
faqs.a: Repointing old stone and lime mortar usually calls for a lime mix that matches the original rather than cement. A trade who works with stone should assess the joints before any patching is done.

faqs.q: I smell gas near the heater in winter. What should I do?
faqs.a: Leave the house and call Australian Gas Networks on 1800 427 532, and call 000 if anyone is in danger. Do not switch anything on or off. Once the supply is made safe, an independent licensed gas fitter can check the heater, flue and connections.

bridgewater.metaDescription: Home repairs in Bridgewater 5155, where stone cottages sit among big mature trees. Roofing, gutters, plumbing and bushfire-season fixes.
bridgewater.h1: Repairs for Bridgewater's Stone Cottages and Big Trees
bridgewater.intro: Bridgewater's houses include older stone cottages and villas around the old mill, often on hilly, heavily treed ground. Big trees can drop limbs and litter onto roofs, and winter wet can find gaps. Briks organises repairs here, arranging for independent trades licensed in SA to do the work, with before and after photos and one invoice.
bridgewater.housing: Housing around Bridgewater includes 19th and early 20th century stone cottages and villas, set on slopes that stay damp through the cooler hills winter. Big trees close to the houses can mean leaf litter, blocked gutters and wet ground at the footings. Repairs here can follow the seasons: wet-weather leaks in winter, and exterior timber and pointing checks in drier months.

trades.note: Roofs in this bushfire-prone setting can need attention. Iron sheets can lift at the fixings, chimney pointing can loosen and valley iron can rust where leaf litter stays wet through winter.
Leaves and bark can fill gutters quickly on these slopes. Overflowing gutters can send water behind fascia boards and down stone walls, so clearing and securing gutters before winter is worthwhile.
Older timber windows and verandah posts in Bridgewater can swell and rot in the wet winter air. Sills, reveals and timber details can need repair or replacement.

Some homes here run on tank water, so pump fittings, first-flush diverters and pressure lines are plumbing items that can need attention. Leaks at the tank base or pump fittings are worth catching early.
Stone and render can benefit from breathable paint, and shaded walls can grow mould and green algae through the wet months. Preparation matters more than the topcoat.

Old cottages can have a mix of original wiring and later additions, and outdoor circuits for pumps or sheds can be affected by damp. An independent licensed electrician can check safety switches and pump power.

issues.title: Winter wet behind stone walls
issues.body: Weeks of wet hills weather can push water into mortar and stone. Soft, crumbly pointing and damp patches inside can be signs. Repointing with a compatible mortar and checking gutters above the wall can help address it.

issues.title: Tree limbs and blocked valleys
issues.body: Big trees close to the roof can drop limbs and bark. Roof valleys and gutters can block, water can back up and rust can start at the laps. Clearing the roof, refixing loose iron and replacing rusted valley sections can be part of the repair.

issues.title: Tank pump and water line faults
issues.body: Low pressure and pumps cutting in and out can occur in tank-water rentals. This can be due to a blocked pump strainer or a stuck first-flush diverter. A licensed plumber can clean, adjust or replace the pump fittings and check the line.

bridgewater.rentals: Rentals around Bridgewater include older stone cottages and small villas, some on tank water. Damp patches after wet weeks, blocked gutters and pumps losing pressure can arise in these rentals. For rental work, the owner or property manager sets how much can be approved, and work beyond that limit is quoted for approval first.

faqs.q: Our tank water pressure has dropped. Is that a plumbing job?
faqs.a: It can be. A blocked pump strainer or first-flush diverter, or a pump that needs adjusting, can cause low pressure. A licensed plumber can clean the fittings and test the line. If the tank itself is leaking at the base, that is also a plumbing repair.

faqs.q: Can a roof repair wait until after the fire danger season?
faqs.a: Loose iron and blocked valleys are best dealt with before the hot, dry months. A roofing trade can refix sheets and clear valleys so embers have less to catch. Plan repairs early rather than waiting for a total fire ban day.

faqs.q: The stone pointing on our cottage is crumbling. What does that involve?
faqs.a: Crumbling pointing is usually repaired by cutting out the soft mortar and repointing with a compatible mortar that lets the stone breathe. An independent licensed trade can do this. It is best done in drier weather so the new mortar cures properly.
